THE BENCHMARK

A vulnerable dependency.
But is the project affected?

VEX-Bench evaluates whether LLM agents can turn a dependency alert into an evidence-backed assessment of real-world exploitability.

Explore the leaderboard Download dataset
ON THIS PAGEWhy VEX-Bench?The taskDatasetEvaluationPaperCitation
01 / MOTIVATION

An alert is only the beginning.

Dependency scanners flag known vulnerabilities. Determining whether those vulnerabilities can actually affect a downstream project requires a deeper look: which code is used, which paths are reachable, and which conditions make an exploit possible.

VEX-Bench studies this cross-repository reasoning. Agents work with complete project snapshots and CVE identifiers, gathering evidence to explain whether a project is affected—and why.

Correctly predicting a verdict is one challenge.
Explaining the right reason is another.
02 / TASK

From code and CVE to a justified verdict.

INPUTProject + CVE

A source snapshot at a fixed commit and a vulnerability identifier.

→
ANALYSISAgent investigation

Inspect dependencies, follow code paths, and retrieve vulnerability details.

→
OUTPUTVerdict + evidence

A status, justification category, and supporting explanation.

Five ground-truth categories

vulnerable

The project is affected by the vulnerability.

code_not_reachable

The vulnerable code cannot be reached along an exploitable execution path.

code_not_present

The vulnerable code is absent from the project’s dependency context.

requires_configuration

Exploitation depends on a configuration the assessed project does not enable.

requires_environment

Exploitation requires environmental conditions absent from the assessed setup.

03 / DATASET

Real projects. Expert annotations.

The paper’s dataset contains 75 manually annotated cases spanning 67 CVEs and 35 projects. Cases are mined from GitHub dependency-related pull requests and reviewed by annotators with software engineering and security experience.

Go30cases
Java25cases
Python20cases

Each case identifies an exact repository commit. The paper dataset is presented as the 2026-05 release. Results remain associated with that release.

04 / EVALUATION

Evaluate both the verdict and the reason.

VULNERABILITY STATUS

Is the project affected?

Binary accuracy, precision, recall, and F1 measure affected / not-affected predictions. Precision, recall, and F1 use the affected class as positive.

JUSTIFICATION

Does the explanation classify correctly?

Accuracy, macro-F1, and weighted-F1 measure fine-grained label predictions. Macro-F1 weights classes equally; weighted-F1 accounts for class frequency.

The paper evaluates each main configuration over three independent runs, with a ten-minute limit per task in isolated Docker environments. The leaderboard preserves recorded means and standard deviations across the three runs.

Tokens and estimated USD cost are per-case averages where available. Paper entries preserve historical cost estimates. Red Hat entries are computed from original outputs using the same evaluator; unknown costs display as —. Prompts and execution settings may differ between experiments. Use the submitter filter and configuration details when comparing results.
